newsitem.title: SPAIN: TISA buy possibility seen neutral for Telefonica.
newsitem.headline: TISA buy possibility seen neutral for Telefonica.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Telefonica were higher on Tuesday, unaffected by reports that the company would buy the state's stake in its international arm Telefonica Internacional (TISA), analysts said.
Telefonica declined to confirm or deny reports it was planning to buy the state's 23.78 percent stake.
The purchase would be more advantageous to the government -- which needs to narrow its deficit -- than to Telefonica, which already owns a controlling stake in TISA, analysts said.
The share price is unlikely to react unless a deal and a price are actually announced, analysts said.

"The truth is that Telefonica doesn't need (another stake) at all. The only advantage for the firm would be if the stake was worth much more than they pay for it, and it could sell it at a profit to a third party. It also means in the longer term that Telefonica has a free hand in what happens at TISA, without the government being there," said an analyst.
At 1000 GMT, Telefonica was up 10 pesetas to 2,360 while the Ibex 35 index of leading stocks was up 27.43 points, or 0.69 percent, to 4,016.53.
A second analyst said that if the sale price were below TISA's market value, it would be advantageous to Telefonica.
"If the government sells its (TISA) stake for under 150 billion pesetas, it's positive for the stock," said Javier Borrachero, telecoms analyst at Banco Central Hispano in Madrid.
"The deal would be good for the government because it could use the money to grapple with the (public sector) deficit," he added.
